name: Theo thBILL
oneLiner: thBILL is Theo Network's NAV-accreting wrapper of Standard Chartered Libeara's tokenized U.S. T-bill fund, mint/redeem gated to KYC-verified institutions.
collateral: Basket of institutional-grade tokenized U.S. Treasury bills; currently 100% tULTRA, a wrapped representation of Standard Chartered Libeara's ULTRA fund (Delta Wellington Ultra Short Treasury On-Chain Fund), managed by Wellington Management, custodied by Standard Chartered, fund administration by FundBridge Capital
pegMechanism: NAV-accreting token (not pegged to $1); price launched at ~$1.00 and appreciates as T-bill yield accrues; KYC-gated mint/redemption processed instantly in USDC, underlying collateral settled within T+4 business days; restricted to institutional and non-U.S. accredited investors

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Re-derived 2026-07-30 from Theo's live documentation and product page: thBILL is a NAV-accreting tokenized claim on a basket of institutional U.S. Treasury funds (tULTRA/ULTRA via Libeara-Wellington-Standard Chartered, plus FILQ via Fidelity International/Sygnum), minted and redeemed only by KYC-verified participants against USDC with no permissionless mint path and no claim on underlying assets for holders. The live stabilization and claim structure is a tokenized T-bill fund share, matching the tbill archetype already recorded; thBILL has no variantOf parent, so no archetypeOverride divergence applies.

routes.reviewNote: Canonical home deployment: thBILL on Ethereum is a pinned 134-byte proxy to implementation 0x325478a069b0dbbdfbee909fa3741f84259ba519 (EIP-1967 impl slot set, admin slot zero, no upgrade path — read 2026-07-20). Theo documents a separate thBILL OFT contract for cross-chain movement.

LayerZero OFT V2 representation of Ethereum-native thBILL: the arbitrum contract is the documented thBILL OFT at the shared CREATE2 address 0xfdd22ce6d1f66bc0ec89b20bf16ccb6670f55a5a (endpoint() = the LayerZero V2 endpoint 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c with peers wired to Ethereum/Base/HyperEVM, read 2026-07-20). The OFT owner/delegate is the Theo 4-of-6 Admin Multisig 0x94877640dd9e6f1e3cb56bf7b5665b7152601295.

LayerZero OFT V2 representation of Ethereum-native thBILL: the base contract is the documented thBILL OFT at the shared CREATE2 address 0xfdd22ce6d1f66bc0ec89b20bf16ccb6670f55a5a (endpoint() = the LayerZero V2 endpoint 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c with peers wired to Ethereum/Base/HyperEVM, read 2026-07-20). The OFT owner/delegate is the Theo 4-of-6 Admin Multisig 0x94877640dd9e6f1e3cb56bf7b5665b7152601295.

LayerZero OFT V2 representation of Ethereum-native thBILL: the hyperevm contract is the documented thBILL OFT at the shared CREATE2 address 0xfdd22ce6d1f66bc0ec89b20bf16ccb6670f55a5a (endpoint() = the LayerZero V2 endpoint 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c with peers wired to Ethereum/Base/HyperEVM, read 2026-07-20). The OFT owner/delegate is the Theo 4-of-6 Admin Multisig 0x94877640dd9e6f1e3cb56bf7b5665b7152601295.

LayerZero OFT V2 representation of Ethereum-native thBILL on Stable (evm chainId 988): the token sits at the same shared CREATE2 address 0xfdd22ce6d1f66bc0ec89b20bf16ccb6670f55a5a and returned symbol thBILL, 6 decimals, totalSupply 35,612,981.743756 (read 2026-07-29 at block 33586875 on rpc.stable.xyz and stable.drpc.org). endpoint() = the LayerZero V2 endpoint deployed on Stable, 0x6f475642a6e85809b1c36fa62763669b1b48dd5b, with peers wired to the Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, and HyperEVM eids; oftVersion() reports the OFT V2 interface and sharedDecimals() = 6. owner() resolves to the Theo 4-of-6 Admin Multisig 0x94877640dd9e6f1e3cb56bf7b5665b7152601295, matching the other OFT legs. The Ethereum OFT Adapter 0xfdd22ce6d1f66bc0ec89b20bf16ccb6670f55a5a escrows this supply, so the Stable leg reallocates from the canonical Ethereum bucket rather than adding to it.

mintAuthority.summary: thBILL issuance is administered through the Theo backend, an Ethereum DEFAULT_ADMIN TimelockController, and the Theo 4-of-6 governance Safe. The canonical token uses a pinned implementation, while every tracked LayerZero OFT deployment resolves owner and delegate control to the same Safe.

controls.label: Theo Network issuance backend
controls.evidence: Theo Network mints/redeems thBILL for KYC-verified institutional and non-US accredited investors against tULTRA collateral, settling in USDC; there is no permissionless or user-collateralized mint route.

controls.label: thBILL DEFAULT_ADMIN TimelockController (minDelay=0)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295049, hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, 0x2bb4b7...) on token 0x5fa487bca6158c64046b2813623e20755091da0b returned true. Contract verified as TimelockController (minDelay=0 confirmed via getMinDelay()). Controlled by Safe 0x94877640... which holds PROPOSER/EXECUTOR/CANCELLER roles per RoleGranted logs at block 25046194.

controls.label: Theo governance Safe (4-of-6, ETH)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295049: getOwners() returned 6 owners; getThreshold() = 4; slot 0 = 0x41675c099f32341bf84bfc5382af534df5c7461a (Safe v1.4.1 singleton). getModulesPaginated returned empty (next=0x1, arr_len=0). This Safe holds PROPOSER/EXECUTOR/CANCELLER on the TimelockController which holds DEFAULT_ADMIN on the thBILL token.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295049, DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on the canonical thBILL token resolves to TimelockController 0x2bb4b7e6e83fa6b77d0143dad631843cb73dca02 with zero minimum delay; its proposer, executor, and canceller authority resolves to the 4-of-6 Theo Safe 0x94877640dd9e6f1e3cb56bf7b5665b7152601295, which had no enabled modules. The 2026-07-20 deployment review confirms the canonical 134-byte pinned proxy implementation 0x325478a069b0dbbdfbee909fa3741f84259ba519 has no upgrade path. It also enumerates the Arbitrum, Base, and HyperEVM LayerZero OFT deployments and resolves each OFT owner and delegate to the same Theo 4-of-6 Safe.

reserveReview.rationale: Re-opened 2026-07-28: theo.xyz/thbill states thBILL holds two institutional underlyings — ULTRA (Wellington Management via Libeara/Standard Chartered) and FILQ (Fidelity International via Sygnum/Chainlink NAV). Theo's 2026-06-30 announcement states a $20M FILQ investment 'now sits inside thBILL' as the second underlying alongside Wellington's fund. Independent coverage (Our Crypto Talk) corroborates the dual-underlying structure and states Theo has not disclosed FILQ's exact basket weight. Docs at docs.theo.xyz/platform/thbill still describe launch composition as solely tULTRA and note further regulated T-bill tokens may be added; they do not publish a current percentage split. tULTRA docs identify ULTRA's asset families (ultra-short U.S. Treasuries, repos, cash) without category weights. No dual-sourced numeric allocation is published, so the full reserve is held as one aggregate basket with basket-needs-split rather than inventing weights (including third-party ~83/17 or ~84/16 estimates).
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Theo product page + FILQ announcement re-opened 2026-07-28; independent Our Crypto Talk corroboration of dual underlyings and undisclosed weight; Theo tULTRA fact sheet for ULTRA asset families
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Both institutional fund legs (tULTRA/ULTRA and FILQ) are identified by issuer product and announcement sources, but the current percentage allocation between them, ULTRA's internal Treasury/repo/cash split, and any cash/USDC buffer are not published with dual-source dated figures.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: Issuer and independent coverage identify two fund underlyings (ULTRA via tULTRA and FILQ) but do not publish a current defensible allocation split or ULTRA sub-category weights; percentage estimates from secondary reports were not dual-sourced and are not stored.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: ULTRA is custodied by Standard Chartered per tULTRA docs; FILQ is accessed through Sygnum per Theo's FILQ announcement. Provider share percentages, segregation, rehypothecation, and thBILL holders' direct legal claim against underlying fund assets are not published in the reviewed sources. Prior 100% Standard Chartered share is removed because the dual-underlying structure makes a single-provider share unsupported.
